name: MA-09
label: Safe D

key_factors: Keating holds a roughly ten-to-one cash-on-hand advantage as the incumbent
District fundamentals favor Democrats, with a D+6 lean and a favorable national environment
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 95 percent
No public polls or expert ratings cover the race
model.rationale: Keating's incumbency, dominant fundraising edge, and a district that has returned him comfortably all point to a wide margin, and markets price a Democratic win near 95 percent with no contrary evidence anywhere in the record.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending for MacAllister or an unusual collapse in Democratic turnout in a low-salience race could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Bill Keating seeks another term in this southeastern Massachusetts district, which leans Democratic by six points and has consistently returned him by wide margins. The fundamentals favor him strongly: incumbency, a favorable environment, and a large financial edge. Keating has raised about $535,000 and holds more than $511,000 on hand, while Republican Tyler MacAllister has raised about $213,000 with roughly $52,000 available. Prediction markets put the Democratic chance near 95 percent.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals and campaign finance. Massachusetts general elections rarely produce competitive House races, and the challenger remains lightly funded and little known. The expected margin is roughly eighteen points for Keating, with uncertainty somewhat elevated given the absence of polling. Any surprise would likely require an unexpected shift against Democrats across the state.
